CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sample Type: Placental tissue (uncultured)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Fetal loss investigation
Clinical Details: Products of conception submitted for chromosomal analysis following pregnancy loss

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Aneuploidy screening for chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured placental tissue. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for polymorphic microsatellite markers specific to chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y. PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak areas were calculated to determine allele ratios.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 14: ABNORMAL - TRISOMY 14 DETECTED
Marker		Location	Allele Pattern	Ratio
D14S122		14q11.2		Triallelic	1:1:1
D14S125		14q23.2		Triallelic	1:1:1
D14S553		14q32.12	Diallelic	2:1
D14S1010	14q32.33	Triallelic	1:1:1
D14S1007	14q32.33	Diallelic	2:1

CHROMOSOME 13: Normal disomic pattern
Two informative markers analyzed

CHROMOSOME 15: Normal disomic pattern
Three informative markers analyzed

CHROMOSOME 16: Normal disomic pattern
Two informative markers analyzed

CHROMOSOME 18: Normal disomic pattern
Three informative markers analyzed

CHROMOSOME 21: Normal disomic pattern
Four informative markers analyzed

CHROMOSOME 22: Normal disomic pattern
Two informative markers analyzed

SEX CHROMOSOMES: Female (XX)
X chromosome markers show normal female pattern
No Y chromosome markers detected

TRIPLOIDY ASSESSMENT: No evidence of triploidy
Allele patterns consistent with diploid cell line with trisomy 14

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates trisomy 14 in this fetal tissue sample. Five informative markers for chromosome 14 show either triallelic patterns (1:1:1 ratio) or diallelic patterns with abnormal 2:1 ratios, confirming the presence of three copies of chromosome 14.

All other chromosomes tested (13, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X) show normal copy number. The sex chromosome complement is female (XX).

Trisomy 14 is a severe chromosomal abnormality that is incompatible with life. It is typically associated with early pregnancy loss, as observed in this case. Most cases of trisomy 14 arise de novo due to meiotic nondisjunction.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Parental blood samples are requested for karyotype analysis to exclude a balanced chromosome rearrangement involving chromosome 14
2. If parental karyotypes are normal, the recurrence risk for future pregnancies is low (approximately 1%)
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results and implications for future pregnancies
4. Prenatal diagnosis should be offered in subsequent pregnancies

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
